questions.question: Which home address should the employee give: the current one, or the one that applies from the first working day? A new hire who is moving from abroad to Switzerland, or the other way, gets a different source tax liability, canton, cross-border questions and tariff code depending on which address counts. The spec treats the home address country as the country of residence without saying for which date.

Does the questionnaire start empty, or does it show the first working day HR already agreed, for the employee to confirm or correct? HR says 'I ask them to confirm it', which suggests HR already has a date. The spec only says the employee 'enters' it. This decides whether HR provides a value that is shown at the start.

Should the employee ever see the derived results (insurance start date, civil status as the fund will receive it, whether they are subject to source tax, the tariff code or the Liechtenstein result), for example before submitting or in the read-only view? Or are these recorded only for HR? The spec says 'recorded for HR' but never says what the employee sees.

For Liechtenstein residents with more than 45 non-return days, the calculator gives the normal tariff code together with 'Unter Vorbehalt des Doppelbesteuerungsabkommens' (subject to the double taxation agreement) (F-zh_source_tax_calculator-ab4e1e, C1Y / Unter Vorbehalt…). The spec records only the normal tariff code and flags only the 'no liability' case. Should the 'subject to the double taxation agreement' note and the HR flag also go with the tariff code in this case?

Liechtenstein residents who return daily, or expect at most 45 non-return days, get no tariff code. Yet they are asked the denomination, whether the spouse works, and all the children questions before the cross-border step, and none of those answers is used. Is that intended, given data minimisation (G-01)? Or should the cross-border questions come first for Liechtenstein residents so the tariff questions can be skipped, and should those answers be discarded on submission?

Child result row 22, and AC-06.4.3 with it: a minor child of a non-married employee who does NOT live in the household (parental custody, alternating care, employee pays more) 'counts with H'. The calculator note F-zh_source_tax_calculator-96658b says a child counts with H only when it lives in the household. Which is right: H or counted without H (A)? The answer changes the tariff letter.

The house number is required for every employee, but the notes say the sources do not cover addresses without one (rural addresses, building names, some foreign addresses). Can the employee submit without a house number, and if so how? As written, these employees cannot submit at all.

If the employee answers 'yes' to having children, must they add at least one child block before they can submit? And is there a maximum number of children? Today an employee could say 'yes' and add no child at all.

D-036 says inapplicable answers 'may be kept' until submission. AC-08.2.1 says they are kept and reappear when the earlier answer is changed back. Is keeping them a requirement or only allowed? Does it also apply if the employee leaves and comes back later in a new session, before submitting?

What are the valid ranges for dates? For example: can the first working day be in the past or far in the future, and must the date of birth (employee and spouse) be in the past or show a minimum age? Without this there are no rejection criteria to test.
The 60-day (Germany) and 45-day (Liechtenstein) questions refer to the calendar year. For someone who starts mid-year, does the employee estimate for the rest of the current year or for a full year?

Which countries can be chosen for the home address, the nationality and the spouse's residence and nationality? Is there an option for stateless people or an unknown nationality? And which of several non-Swiss nationalities should the employee enter?

Some example tables use the same item as both input and expected output (AC-08.4.2 lists 'Nationality' twice; AC-05.4.3 has 'Spouse / partner is gainfully employed…' as input and output 'asked'). Which value is the expected result, so the examples can be tested?

already_flagged: OQ-canton-abroad: what to enter in the fund's 'Canton' field for employees living abroad, and whether it means canton of residence or work (the US-01.4 title already assumes residence)
OQ-civil-status-partnership: how the fund registers registered partnerships and separated employees
OQ-spouse-dob-other-status: whether Divorced or Widowed need extra fund fields
OQ-calculator-coverage: unverified paths (residence block for A/B/H, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N, child rows marked inferred)
OQ-nationality-wording: ask nationality as a country or only 'Swiss citizen yes/no', and whether the dual-citizenship rule applies to the spouse

tech_leaks.quote: Step 7 'Children' – one block per child, repeated for each child the employee adds; all child_* conditions refer to the same child.
tech_leaks.why: 'child_*' is an internal field-id prefix used in prose. Business readers should not see identifier naming.

tech_leaks.quote: Afterwards Step 9 'Finish': permit reminder (rule permit_reminder), then submission
tech_leaks.why: Uses an internal rule id ('permit_reminder') in prose instead of the business name of the rule.

tech_leaks.quote: When Lonio has decided whether the employee is subject to source tax (rule subject_to_source_tax)
tech_leaks.why: Uses an internal rule identifier in an acceptance criterion. That is an implementation artifact, not business language.

tech_leaks.quote: (The formal expression covers one child block; the digit is the sum over all children.)
tech_leaks.why: Refers to how the rule is encoded (a 'formal expression' per child block). That is an implementation detail of the rule engine, not a business statement.

tech_leaks.quote: the employee goes through one block of questions per child and can add another child or remove one
tech_leaks.why: Prescribes the interaction (repeatable blocks with add and remove controls, copied from the calculator UI). The need is only to capture each child's answers.

tech_leaks.quote: their answers are kept, so that if the employee changes the earlier answer back, the earlier input reappears and need not be entered again
tech_leaks.why: Turns D-036's permissive 'may be kept' into required draft-retention and re-display behaviour, which is an implementation choice.
